subject: Model Supply, Trust & Licensing Assertions — RFP follow-up and attachments
messages:
From: Dana Li <dana.li@acmecorp.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFP follow-up: provenance, attribution, and pinning controls

Hi Rafael,

Thanks for the initial RFP packet. We have a few clarifying asks related to your model catalog and licensing assertions before we finalize the procurement packet:

1) For each curated model in the Redwood catalog, can you provide the license type and an immutable pointer to the original source (commit hash, download URL, or package identifier)?
2) Do you provide a signed SBOM / provenance artifact that includes training data provenance at a high level and binary fingerprints?
3) What is your recommended version-pinning strategy for production deployments (how do you guarantee a pinned model stays unchanged, and what is your update/deprecation notification cadence)?
4) In the event of license changes upstream, what is the notification process and the rollback/fallback options you support?

We plan to include these answers in our security/compliance appendix — if you can attach any manifests or templates, that would be helpful.

Best,
Dana Li
Procurement — Acme Corporation
attachments: none

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 01 Oct 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: RFP follow-up: provenance, attribution, and pinning controls

Marissa / Karthik — forwarding Acme's follow-up (excerpt above). They want concrete artifacts and formal language for the procurement appendix. I drafted quick bullets below that I think are safe to send but need legal/compliance sign-off on a couple of lines (esp. around attestations and "signed SBOM"). Also thinking we should include the inventory CSV and our pinning playbook.

DRAFT bullet answers for Acme:
- License mapping: Each curated model in the Redwood catalog is accompanied by a license field in the catalog UI and in the model manifest. We map upstream licenses to a normalized license taxonomy (e.g., MIT, Apache-2.0, GPL variants, proprietary) in column "license_id".
- Immutable source pointers: For open models we store the canonical upstream source URL and a commit hash or release tag where available. For third-party binaries we include cryptographic checksums (SHA256) in the manifest.
- Provenance artifacts: We produce a model manifest (CSV + JSON) that includes source pointer, checksum, model architecture, quantization profile, and a signer identity. For customers on Dedicated / Private we can provide an attestable artifact signed by Redwood's release key.
- SBOM and training data: We provide an SBOM-like manifest for third-party components and a high-level provenance summary for training corpora (supplier names, public datasets used). We do not disclose customer training data or PII; any dataset-level attestations are high-level.
- Pinning strategy: Customers can pin model versions by manifest-id (manifest_v3 ID) — the pinned manifest is immutable in the catalog. When a new upstream release occurs, customers receive a notification and we create a new manifest; the customer must opt into an update.
- Update/Deprecation: For breaking updates (licenses or behavior changes) Redwood will notify subscribed customers 30 days prior to enforced rollover; critical security patches may have shorter windows but will include rollback instructions and a temporary compatible fallback model when available.

Can you both review and add legal-safe language for the "signed SBOM" and "attestable artifact" lines? I can incorporate and send final to Acme next week.

— Rafael
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 04 Oct 2027 11:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: RFP follow-up: provenance, attribution, and pinning controls

Rafael / Karthik — quick notes from compliance: we should avoid the phrase "signed SBOM" unless Legal can confirm the signing key scope. Suggested edits inline below (I pasted Rafael's bullets and added bracketed notes):

- License mapping: OK. Add: "Redwood provides a downloadable license matrix mapping catalog entries to upstream license text and SPDX identifiers."
- Immutable source pointers: OK. Add: "Where upstream authors publish a VCS commit or release tag, we reference that exact identifier; otherwise we include the download URL plus SHA256."
- Provenance artifacts: Replace "signed SBOM" with: "attested model manifest" and clarify that attestations are produced by Redwood's release automation and include a signature metadata field; formal cryptographic signing (PKI-signed artifacts) is available for Redwood Dedicated / Private deployments under an MSA addendum.
- SBOM and training data: Keep high-level. Add: "We can provide vendor-supplied dataset manifest references for open datasets; no customer data is included."
- Pinning strategy: Add: "Pinning is by immutable manifest_id; manifests are immutable once published to the catalog and are retained for audit purposes."
- Update/Deprecation: Add: "Notifications are sent via console, API webhook, and e-mail to subscribed contacts. Customers may opt into automatic minor updates; major updates are opt-in by default."

Karthik — can you confirm we have the release automation metadata field names we use for signatures (e.g., signer_id, signature_algo, signature_value) so I can include exact keys in the manifest sample? If Legal needs a template, I can attach the playbook + manifest sample.

— Marissa
Senior Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Dana Li <dana.li@acmecorp.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 05 Oct 2027 16:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: provenance, attribution, and pinning controls

Dana — thanks for the clear asks. Please find our formal responses below and attached artifacts (manifest CSV, license matrix, pinning playbook). We have kept the language concise for inclusion in your appendix; happy to jump on a call if you want to walk through the manifests.

Redwood responses (summary):

1) License & source pointers
- Each catalog entry includes: license_id (SPDX), upstream_source (URL), source_tag_or_commit (if available), and checksum_sha256 for distributed binaries. See attached license-matrix-2027Q3.xlsx for a crosswalk.

2) Attested manifests and provenance
- We provide a machine-readable model manifest (CSV + JSON) that contains metadata fields: manifest_id, model_name, model_version, architecture, quantization_profile, upstream_source, source_tag_or_commit, checksum_sha256, signer_id, signature_algo, signature_value, published_at.
- For Hosted customers we produce attestation metadata; for Dedicated/Private customers we can deliver PKI-signed artifacts under an addendum. The attached Model-Inventory-Manifest_v3.csv is an example export.

3) Pinning and immutability
- Pinning is performed at manifest_id. Manifest records are immutable once published to the catalog for auditability. Customers may pin a manifest_id via Console, API, or as part of deployment config; pinning guarantees the served weights and quantization profile remain unchanged.

4) Updates, notification & rollback
- Notification channels: console banner, API webhook subscription, and e-mail to subscribed contacts.
- Update cadence: non-breaking/patch updates are announced and may be auto-applied if the customer opts in. Major releases or license changes follow a minimum 30-day notification period. Critical security fixes may be expedited (shorter notice) with a recommended rollback path and temporary compatibility fallback models.

5) License-change events and fallback
- If an upstream license changes incompatibly, Redwood will: (a) create a new manifest for the re-licensed artifact; (b) flag the prior manifest as "retired" with a retention window for audits; (c) notify affected customers and provide recommended fallback manifests where available. Customers retain control to keep existing pinned manifests.

Attachments included:
- Model-Inventory-Manifest_v3.csv (sample manifest with metadata columns)
- pinning-playbook.pdf (customer-facing guidance on pinning & rollouts)
- license-matrix-2027Q3.xlsx (catalog license crosswalk)

If you'd like, we can append a short paragraph to this language that references Redwood's SOC 2 controls and audit logging for manifest access. Would that be helpful for your compliance appendix?

Regards,
Rafael Mendes
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
